subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Hi Jordan / FinLytics team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to walk through your real-time trading assistant workload. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we can validate p95/p99 end-to-end latency and compare Redwood hosted vs your current provider.

Quick recap (what we heard):
- Target end-to-end latency (client SDK call -> last token received): p95 <= 1,000 ms, p99 <= 2,000 ms for single-turn prompts; multi-turn flows can tolerate p95 up to 1,500 ms.
- Expected payload profile: avg prompt length ~120 tokens, typical response ~80 tokens, 95th percentile response length ~300 tokens.
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained 500 qps, burst up to 2,000 qps for short windows; concurrency per session ~3-10.
- Streaming: partial token streaming required (user should see first tokens within 200-300 ms ideally).

Open questions we flagged for validation:
1) Measurement point: confirm you want end-to-end (SDK -> last token), not just inference kernel time.
2) Warm vs cold state: are you ok with initial warm-up behavior? Do you have any strict cold-start SLOs?
3) Allowed fallbacks: should we consider model-variant fallbacks (smaller quantized models) when latency spikes?

Proposed next steps (how Redwood can help):
- We will run a targeted perf test in our hosted staging with your representative prompt set (you to share sample prompts & token-length distribution).
- Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, tail-latency breakdown (client SDK, edge, network, inference), throughput stability graphs, and a test-run artifact (csv). See attached redwood-p95-p99-matrix.pdf for format.
- Timing: propose a 48-hour test window next week (May 18-19) to capture steady-state + burst.
- Follow-up: schedule a technical sync with your infra + security folks to confirm measurement instrumentation and access.

If that looks good I can have Marissa run the perf-plan and we’ll send the onboarding checklist (keys, staging endpoints, rate-limiter settings).

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-p95-p99-matrix.pdf (1.2MB stub)

From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Laura —

Thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Measurement: yes, end-to-end as you described. We want the user-perceived latency measured from our browser client SDK invocation to the last character rendered.
- Targets: for single-turn we can be flexible — p95 <= 1s and p99 <= 2s is our hard ask for the most latency-sensitive flows (trade confirmations). For multi-turn, the p99 up to 2.5s is acceptable.
- Streaming: critical. If you can ensure first-byte streaming within ~250ms for short responses that will meet UX goals.

One procurement note — we need a breakdown vs our current vendor showing typical delta at p95/p99 for similar prompt sizes. Also our security team will want to confirm data handling for hosted tests (we can use anonymized prompts).

I’ll collect sample prompts and send over later today. Also looping in our infra lead (eng@finlytics.com) who will coordinate the staging access.

—Jordan
Sr. PM, FinLytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted vs current provider - postcall recap

Jordan / team —

Appreciate the clarifications. A few technical details to set expectations for the perf run and how we’ll compare against your current provider: 

1) Measurement definitions (end-to-end):
- Client SDK start timestamp: when SDK issues POST (or ws open) to Redwood endpoint.
- First-byte: when first token chunk delivered to client (stream flush).
- Last-byte: when the final token for that request is received.
We will report p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and last-byte.

2) Warm vs cold:
- Our hosted staging will be warmed before the main window to approximate steady-state. We will also capture a cold-start sample set (first 50 requests) and label them. If you have strict cold-start SLOs call them out and we’ll include separately.

3) Streaming behavior:
- Redwood supports chunked streaming (HTTP/2 + SSE / WebSocket). For short responses we can flush partial output once the top-k decoding produces stable tokens; typical first-byte times in hosted tests are ~120-300ms depending on model & tokenization.

4) Throughput/Concurrency test plan (high level):
- Steady-state: 500 qps sustained for 2 hours with realistic interleaving of prompt lengths.
- Burst window: 2,000 qps for 5 minutes to evaluate tail latency/backpressure.
- Concurrency per session: emulate 3-10 concurrent in-flight requests per user.

5) Comparison vs current provider:
- We will run the same test harness against your current provider endpoints (you to provide staging keys) and produce a side-by-side p50/p95/p99 table plus tail-latency waterfall.

Attachments included: test-plan-finlytics.csv (payload permutations + sequencing), redwood-p95-p99-matrix.pdf (expected report format).

Next steps / action items:
- Jordan: share anonymized prompt set + staging keys for current provider.
- FinLytics Eng: confirm time window (we proposed May 18-19).
- Laura/Marissa: we’ll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff to walk the test harness and SLO measurement points.

If we get your sample prompts today we’ll prep the harness and send a run checklist (rate limits, client SDK flags).

Thanks,
Marissa
Perf & Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: test-plan-finlytics.csv (stub), redwood-p95-p99-matrix.pdf (stub)
